-2-  NC: 2023:KHC:34381  MFA No. 7620 of 2015  THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

In this appeal, the petitioner has challenged the judgment dated 03.09.2015 passed in M.V.C.No.839/2013 by the Senior Civil Judge and Additional M.A.C.T., Kundapura ('the Tribunal'
in short).
2.
For the sake of convenience, the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are, on 14.05.2013 at about 07:30 pm, while the petitioner was travelling as a pillion rider in a motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 20/U-6062 from Shankaranarayana towards Haladi side near R.F.O., Shankaranarayana, the rider had lost the control over the motor cycle and turtled on the road, due to which the petitioner has sustained head injury and he was admitted to K.M.C. Hospital, NC: 2023:KHC:34381 Manipal and has undergone surgery.
Seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/-, he has approached the Tribunal.
Claim was opposed by the Insurance Company.
After taking the evidence, the Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.3,41,673/- with interest of 6% p.a.
Pleading inadequacy and seeking enhancement of compensation, the petitioner has filed this appeal on various grounds.

4. Heard the arguments of Ms. Thanima Bekal, learned counsel for the petitioner and Smt. Manjula.
N. Tejaswi, learned counsel for the Insurance Company.
5.
It is the contention of the leaned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner has suffered closed head injury with multiple contusion on the left side of third nerve palsy.

He has sustained 45.16%
cognitive disability.

Taking into consideration the income as Rs.15,000/- per month and 45%
disability, the compensation may be assessed.
It is NC: 2023:KHC:34381 also contended that compensation awarded under pain and suffering and loss of amenities and discomfort is on the lower side.
6. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has contended that no doubt, the petitioner has sustained head injury and cognitive disability which may reduce his future earning capacity.
Taking into consideration this aspect, the Tribunal has rightly considered the disability of 20%.
Since the petitioner has not produced any proof of income, the Tribunal has taken the income at Rs.6,500/-.

Learned counsel is fair enough that in the year 2013, before Lok Adalat, income of a person with no proof of income is taken at Rs.8,000/- and she fairly submitted that loss of income Sri Manjunatha Acharya vs Sri Chandra Acharya on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175167068/
2 due to disability may be calculated taking the income of the petitioner at Rs.8,000/-.

sentences.text: It is also submitted that the enhancement of compensation NC: 2023:KHC:34381 may be considered globally including the interest portion.
7. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on both sides and also perused the materials on record.
8. The material on record points out the injury sustained by the petitioner is 'closed head injury with multiple contusion in left 3rd nerve palsy'.
He was under hospitalization.
Ex.P1 is the disability certificate issued by Kasturba Hospital, Manipal referring 45.16% of disability sustained by the injured on account of the head injury.
Ex.P1 refers to NIMHANS neuropsychological battery resulting 45.16% of cognitive disability.

PW-1 Dr. Haridas, who is the Assistant Professor,
Department of Psychiatry, Kasturba Hospital, Manipal, in the course of cross-examination, has narrated that the petitioner having deficiency in memory, he cannot concentrate on a single work while shifting one NC: 2023:KHC:34381 aspect to other, thereby he could not immediately change over his attitude and therefore, he has assessed the disability.
The material on record did point out that the nature of disability though assessed on that particular point of time, on the days to come there are chances of reduction.
Under these circumstances, the assessment of disability at 45.16% is rightly not accepted by the Tribunal.
Having regard to circumstances and gravity of the injury, the disability has to be assessed at 25% instead of 20% assessed by the Tribunal.
The accident is of the year 2013.
A person with no proof of income in 2013 will not earn less than Rs.8,000/- per month and therefore, notional income has to be taken at Rs.8,000/- instead of Rs.6,500/-.
If that is considered, having regard to pain and sufferings, Rs.40,000/- has to be awarded and also loss of amenities and discomfort at Rs.12,000/-.
I am of the opinion that enhancement is required on these heads.

Adverting to the arguments of learned counsel for the Insurance Company for assessment of global compensation, the petitioner has no objection if global compensation is awarded including the interest component.

Having regard to discussions made above, in spite of assessing the compensation on different heads, I am of the opinion that a global compensation of Rs.5,50,000/-
including the interest component could be awarded as enhancement in addition to what has been assessed by the Tribunal.
Accordingly, the appeal merits consideration, in the result, the following:

ORDER i) The appeal is allowed in part.
ii) Impugned judgment is modified.

iii) The petitioner is entitled to global compensation of Rs.5,50,000/-
including interest component in addition to the award of the Tribunal.
